name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  April 6, 2015

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Schlicht at 5:01 p.m., on April 6, 2015, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on April 1, 2015, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Sachs
  Council Member Ury
  Mayor Pro Tem Raths
  Mayor Schlicht

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, Assistant City Clerk

RECESS

At the hour of 5:02 p.m., Mayor Schlicht declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 6:09
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that CS1 dealt with labor and employment matters. The
Council advised its negotiators but no reportable action was taken. CS2 addressed a variety of
pending legal issues with no reportable action however, the council gave direction for future
implementation.

City Council Minutes  1  April 6, 2015
 INVOCATION: Council Member Ury

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Bucknum

PRESENTATIONS

  P1.  Library Card Design Contest Winners

  Mayor Schlicht presented certificates of commendation to Jacki Long, Meena Jolly,
  Morgan Tieu, Tyler Phan, and Alaina Klaes.

  P2.  Recognize the Recipients of the Art-X-Press Scholarship

  Mayor Schlicht presented certificate of commendation to Grace Fisher from Los Alisos
  Middle School.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Charles McCollough, M.V.: shared a listing of Chamber of Commerce events for the month of
April, including the monthly mixer, and weekly networking meetings.

Larry Gilbert, M.V.: spoke about the Nadadores facility and raised concerns about the cost to the
City to replace the dive tower.

Gary Wertz, M.V.: voiced his concerns over the need to renovate the shopping center across from
City Hall.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and
  further reading waived.

 2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the Regular Meeting of March 16, 2015, as presented.

City Council Minutes  2  April 6, 2015
  3.  Check Register Dated March 6, 2015 in the Amount of $910,788.33

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

 4.  Check Register Dated March 13, 2015 in the Amount of $520,430.46

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

 5.  Check Register Dated March 20, 2015 in the Amount of $1,654,938.45

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

 6.  Amendment to the Waste Disposal Agreement Between the County of Orange and
  the City of Mission Viejo

  (1) Adopted Resolution 15-14 Approving an Amendment to the 2009 Waste Disposal
  Agreement with the County of Orange; and (2) authorized the Mayor to execute the
  Amendment on behalf of the City of Mission Viejo.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

OLD BUSINESS

Items 7 and 15 were considered together.

 7.  SDG&E’s Request for Support – South Orange County Reliability Enhancement
  Project

 15.  Consideration of a Resolution Opposing Negative Impacts of the proposed San Diego
  Gas and Electric (SDG&E) South Orange County Reliability Enhancement Project
  Unless Fully Mitigated

  City Manager Dennis Wilberg presented the staff report for Item 7.

  Mayor Schlicht presented her report for Item 15.

  Larry Gilbert, M.V: speaking on behalf of Joe Holtzman who could not attend the
  meeting, Mr. Gilbert read an email from Mr. Holtzman voicing opposition to the project.

  R. Kohan, Kathleen Petersen, and Pedro Villanueba, San Juan Capistrano: spoke in
  opposition to the project and in favor of Mayor Schlicht’s recommendation.

  Duane Cave of SDG&E answered the City Council Member’s questions about the
  SOCRE project.

City Council Minutes  3  April 6, 2015
 RECESS

At the hour of 7:10 p.m., Mayor Schlicht declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 7:20
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, Seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Raths to approve
  a letter of support for SDG&E’s South Orange County Reliability Enhancement project,
  and send the letter to the California Public Utilities Commission.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, and Ury
  NOES:  Sachs and Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

  *Mayor Schlicht withdrew item #15.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

  8.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Sachs presented the report and raised concerns about a letter that was
  sent to Assemblyman Brough regarding the City’s opposition to Assembly Bill 1217
  (the restructuring of the OCFA Board of Directors.) He questioned why the Council did
  not discuss this matter at a City Council Meeting.

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: voiced his opposition to AB1217.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Raths to approve
  the letter that was sent to Assemblyman Brough and to return at the next City Council
  Meeting on April 20, 2015, for further discussion and input on AB1217.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

 9.  Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Council Member Ury presented the report.

 10.  Renewal of Rental Permit with Outta Bounds Events for Use of the Thomas R.
  Potocki Conference Center for Fiscal Year 2015-2016

  Director of Recreation and Community Services Mark Nix presented the report.

City Council Minutes  4  April 6, 2015
   Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Schlicht to renew the
  rental permit with Outta Bounds Events for use of the Thomas R. Potocki Conference
  Center for Fiscal Year 2015-2016 in the amount of $6,000.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

STAFF REPORTS

 11.  FY 2015-17 Revenue Projections

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  By consensus, the City Council received the report.

 12.  Update on Contract Preparation for Service Contracts

  City Manager Dennis Wilberg presented the staff report.

  Scott Griffiths, Great Scott Tree Service: spoke in favor of the City issuing an RFP for
  city-wide tree trimming services.

  Pat Mahoney, West Coast Arborists: expressed support for the extension of West Coast
  Arborists’ agreement in lieu of going out to bid.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to
  extend the current agreement with West Coast Arborists for an additional eight (8) years
  with the full understanding that WCA will honor current rates for the first two years of
  the extension and at that time the City can either negotiate new rates or terminate the
  agreement.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

 13.  Campout on the Oso Creek Trail Program Fee

  Director of Recreation and Community Services Mark Nix presented the report.

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to
  continue the event with no fees for participants.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
City Council Minutes  5  April 6, 2015
   AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

26.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented
  in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum announced that she attended the League of California Cities Orange
County Division General Membership Meeting in Irvine. She also attended the Pillars Academy
Banquet with Mayor Pro Tem Raths for the recognition of Teacher Faieza Hadi. Ms. Hadi received
the Director’s award for her fifteen-year commitment to establishing a strong foundation for
students in English, Arabic and Islamic values at Pillars Academy. She was also honored by O.C.
Parenting Magazine as one of the top 25 educators across public and private schools in all of
Orange County. Council Member Bucknum discussed her attendance at the volunteer appreciation
for the Mission Viejo Activities Committee and the CPUC public hearing in San Clemente where
she spoke in support. Council Member Bucknum and Council Member Ury attended the CUSD ad
hoc committee meeting to discuss specific schools that are impacted by traffic issues, as well as
the sharing of facilities and park issues specifically related to Bathgate Elementary School. She
also attended a Work Force Score Card Housing Workshop that was put on by the Orange County
Business Council and she commented that the housing in Orange County has a direct impact on
the ability to have economic growth and development. Council Member Bucknum stated that she
is proud to announce that she was appointed as Co-Chair of the ACC-OC's Economic
Development Committee and to the SCAG Committee on Community Economic and Human
Development. She stated that Mission Viejo has a unique responsibility as one of the largest cities
in south Orange County and it should be a part of the success. She is glad the City is going to be
in the mix and hopefully bring some of those businesses and developments to Mission
Viejo. Council Member Bucknum mentioned her attendance at Bunny Days and she announced
that Relay for Life is looking for teams so she encouraged residents to sign up. She noted that on
Saturday April 25, Hopeful Healing for Survivors is having a 5k Run/Walk Health & Safety Expo
at Mason Park in Irvine and she closed her comments by complimenting Orange County Register
reporter Tomoya Shimura on his recent article on the Marguerite Swim Complex.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs thanked Mayor Pro Tem Raths for nominating him as Vice Chairman of
the Toll Roads Operations Committee. He also gave a “shout out” to 90 year-old residents Ann
and Rose whom he recently met during the Meals on Wheels delivery program.

City Council Minutes  6  April 6, 2015
 Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury outlined his attendance at the OCBC meeting where the topic of the housing
supply shortage and the crushing of the middle class in California was discussed. He also attended
the CUSD ad hoc meeting with Council Member Bucknum and he said he felt it was a good initial
step. By giving staff direction, he hopes that some of the topics they discussed will be brought to
the Council before the middle of the year. The Council can consider enacting policy for joint use
of the fields and in turn, the City can either maintain or utilize some of the school’s bathrooms to
cut down on costs. Council Member Ury announced that he visited the Carlsbad Desalinization
Plant which has been 12 years in the making and it is scheduled to come online in November,
possibly as early as April. He also announced that his term as President of the ACCOC is ending
on Thursday and Tustin Council Member Al Murray will be the new President. Council Member
Ury invited his colleagues to the transition ceremony at the Tustin City Hall.

Mayor Pro Tem Raths

Mayor Pro Tem Raths discussed drought concerns and stated that he has attended several of the
water board meetings throughout south Orange County. He asked staff to look into the Proposition
1 Water Bond to so see if Mission Viejo can qualify for any of the grants. Mayor Pro Tem Raths
announced that he applied for the Santa Margarita Water District’s turf removal rebate which gives
residents $2 for every square foot of turf removed and replaced with drought tolerant plants. Lastly,
Mayor Pro Tem Raths shared a video of Governor Jerry Brown discussing the topic of the
California drought.

Mayor Schlicht

Mayor Schlicht commented on the Governor’s new executive order and she stated that she feels
we need solutions not regulations. She said that infrastructure statewide is inadequate, which is
an indication that the state government has failed.

Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay responded that three landscape
areas will be affected by the mandate. The 25 percent reduction is for domestic water use. The City
has three areas that are regulated by domestic water: south Marguerite Parkway to the south of
Crown Valley Parkway, Trabuco Road and Marguerite Parkway, and Vista Del Lago north. Mr.
Rattay noted that staff is preparing a blog article to inform residents that these areas will have the
water turned off and to expect brown grass. Mr. Rattay reiterated that re-cycled water is not
affected by the new executive order.

Mayor Schlicht asked how much of the City’s landscaping is irrigated with recycled water and Mr.
Rattay responded that it will be over 80 percent after this summer’s project in Califia is complete.
Mayor Schlicht voiced her concern over the Marguerite Swim Complex pool repairs and Mr.
Rattay responded that he is working with the water districts regarding this project.

Mayor Schlicht clarified a question that was brought up at a Community Services Commission
Meeting challenging her comment that the current pool that the Nadadores use was obsolete. She
wanted the Commissioners to know that she received this information from the Nadadores. It was
in their report to the Commission on June 21, 2011, in an RFP for re-use of the Murray Center. In
the report to the City it was noted that the International Governing Body for Swimming had

City Council Minutes  7  April 6, 2015
 recently decided on the use of 10-lane pools for their sanctioned events was required. Mayor
Schlicht announced that she is happy that the Angels are back in season and she congratulated the
City’s high school softball and hardball teams that are ranked in the nation. Mayor Schlicht
questioned the parking fee regulations at the high schools and asked that the City Attorney research
Vehicle Code section 2113. She congratulated the Library Card Design Contest winners as well as
the ArtXPress Scholarship recipients who were recognized earlier in the meeting. Mayor Schlicht
stated that it is always good to be recognized for artistic talents and with all the budget cuts in the
schools, it’s good to see organizations like the library offering opportunities for students to express
themselves and to see the Pacific Symphony offering scholarships for music and the arts. Mayor
Schlicht thanked Council Member Sachs for raising concern about the City’s letters of support or
opposition and in closing, she quoted George Washington: “There is a rank due to the United States
among nations which will be withheld if not absolutely lost by the reputation of weakness. If we
desire to avoid insult we must be able to repel it. If we desire to secure peace, one of the most
powerful instruments of our rising prosperity it must be known that we are at all times ready for
war.”

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:00 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Schlicht adjourned the meeting to Monday, April 20, 2015, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Kimberly Schmitt, Assistant City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of April 20, 2015

City Council Minutes  8  April 6, 2015
